review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

4:1.sourceText: Ἰησοῦς δὲ πλήρης Πνεύματος Ἁγίου ὑπέστρεψεν ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ ἤγετο ἐν τῷ Πνεύματι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ
4:1.targetText: Then Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,

4:2.sourceText: ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου. Καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις, καὶ συντελεσθεισῶν αὐτῶν ἐπείνασεν.
4:2.targetText: where for forty days He was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they had ended, He was hungry.

groups.note: The accusative ἡμέρας expresses duration ("for … days").
The Greek double negative οὐκ … οὐδέν ("not … nothing") makes one English negative.
The genitive absolute συντελεσθεισῶν αὐτῶν ("they having ended") is rendered as a when-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English relative linking back to the wilderness of 4:1; the Greek continues with a participle.

4:3.sourceText: εἶπεν δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, εἰπὲ τῷ λίθῳ τούτῳ ἵνα γένηται ἄρτος.
4:3.targetText: The devil said to Him, “If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unrendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:4.sourceText: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς Γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἐπ’ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ὁ ἄνθρωπος.
4:4.targetText: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’”

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτόν ("to him") unrendered after answered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the colon and quotation marks.

4:5.sourceText: Καὶ ἀναγαγὼν αὐτὸν ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐν στιγμῇ χρόνου.
4:5.targetText: Then the devil led Him up to a high place and showed Him in an instant all the kingdoms of the world.

groups.note: The participle ἀναγαγών ("having led up") is rendered as a finite verb.
στιγμῇ χρόνου ("a point of time") is rendered an instant.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle and verb.
English supplies a destination for "led up"; the Greek names no place here.
English joins the participle clause to "showed".

4:6.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος Σοὶ δώσω τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἅπασαν καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐμοὶ παραδέδοται καὶ ᾧ ἐὰν θέλω δίδωμι αὐτήν·
4:6.targetText: “I will give You authority over all these kingdoms and all their glory,” he said. “For it has been relinquished to me, and I can give it to anyone I wish.

groups.note: BSB renders ὁ διάβολος ("the devil") as he, the devil having been named in 4:5.
ταύτην ("this") qualifies the authority in Greek; BSB applies it to the kingdoms.
ἅπασαν ("all of it") qualifies the authority in Greek.
ᾧ ἐάν ("to whomever") is rendered to anyone.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unrendered with said.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English links the authority to its domain.
English names the kingdoms of 4:5 as the domain of the authority.
English repeats "all" before glory; the Greek has it only with the authority.

4:7.sourceText: σὺ οὖν ἐὰν προσκυνήσῃς ἐνώπιον ἐμοῦ, ἔσται σοῦ πᾶσα.
4:7.targetText: So if You worship me, it will all be Yours.”

unmappedSource.reason: ἐνώπιον ("before") is absorbed in the transitive English "worship me".

4:8.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ Γέγραπται Προσκυνήσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.
4:8.targetText: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς … εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unrendered after answered.

4:9.sourceText: Ἤγαγεν δὲ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἱερουσαλὴμ καὶ ἔστησεν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ Εἰ Υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ Θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν ἐντεῦθεν κάτω·
4:9.targetText: Then the devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple. “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down from here.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB places "he said" inside the quotation and leaves καί unrendered.
BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unrendered with said.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb.
English object of set; the Greek ἔστησεν has none here.

4:10.sourceText: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ τοῦ διαφυλάξαι σε,
4:10.targetText: For it is written:  ‘He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully;

groups.note: τοῦ with the infinitive διαφυλάξαι ("to guard closely") expresses purpose; carefully renders the intensive δια-.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the colon and quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:11.sourceText: καὶ ὅτι ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε μή ποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.
4:11.targetText: and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’”

groups.note: μή ποτε ("lest") marks the negative purpose clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The second ὅτι introducing the next quoted line is not rendered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the possessor of hands; the Greek has none.

4:12.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Εἴρηται Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις Κύριον τὸν Θεόν σου.
4:12.targetText: But Jesus answered, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’”

groups.note: ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ("answering, said") is rendered by one verb.
Εἴρηται ("it has been said") is rendered It says.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves αὐτῷ ("to him") unrendered after answered.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the quotation marks.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds "also" to mark the second quotation; the Greek has no "again" here.

4:13.sourceText: Καὶ συντελέσας πάντα πειρασμὸν ὁ διάβολος ἀπέστη ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι καιροῦ.
4:13.targetText: When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Him until an opportune time.

groups.note: The participle συντελέσας ("having finished") is rendered as a when-clause.
ἀπέστη ἀπ’ ("departed from") is rendered left.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.

4:14.sourceText: Καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ Πνεύματος εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν· καὶ φήμη ἐξῆλθεν καθ’ ὅλης τῆς περιχώρου περὶ αὐτοῦ.
4:14.targetText: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and the news about Him spread throughout the surrounding region.

groups.note: καθ’ ὅλης ("throughout the whole") is rendered throughout.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:15.sourceText: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδίδασκεν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν, δοξαζόμενος ὑπὸ πάντων.
4:15.targetText: He taught in their synagogues and was glorified by everyone.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to "taught".

4:16.sourceText: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἰς Ναζαρά, οὗ ἦν τεθραμμένος, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν κατὰ τὸ εἰωθὸς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν, καὶ ἀνέστη ἀναγνῶναι.
4:16.targetText: Then Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up. As was His custom, He entered the synagogue on the Sabbath. And when He stood up to read,

groups.note: εἰσῆλθεν … εἰς ("went into") is rendered entered.
τὸ εἰωθός ("what was customary") is an article with a participle, rendered custom.
ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων ("the day of the Sabbaths") is rendered Sabbath.
BSB turns "and He stood up … and the scroll was handed" into "And when He stood up …, the scroll … was handed".

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.
Supplied copula in "As was His custom".

4:17.sourceText: καὶ ἐπεδόθη αὐτῷ βιβλίον τοῦ προφήτου Ἡσαΐου, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ βιβλίον εὗρεν τὸν τόπον οὗ ἦν γεγραμμένον
4:17.targetText: the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him. Unrolling it, He found the place where it was written:

groups.note: N1904 has ἀνοίξας ("opening"); BSB follows a different verb with the same meaning, since opening a scroll is unrolling it.
τὸ βιβλίον ("the scroll") is rendered it.

unmappedSource.reason: This καί joins "stood up" and "was handed"; BSB expresses that sequence with the "And when" that closes 4:16.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

4:18.sourceText: Πνεῦμα Κυρίου ἐπ’ ἐμέ, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέν με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, ἀπέσταλκέν με κηρῦξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν καὶ τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει,
4:18.targetText: “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,

groups.note: οὗ εἵνεκεν ("on account of which") is rendered because.
ἀποστεῖλαι … ἐν ἀφέσει ("to send away in release") is rendered to release.

unmappedTarget.reason: Supplied copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

4:19.targetText: to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”

groups.note: The adjective δεκτόν ("acceptable") is rendered "of … favor".

4:20.sourceText: καὶ πτύξας τὸ βιβλίον ἀποδοὺς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ ἐκάθισεν· καὶ πάντων οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦσαν ἀτενίζοντες αὐτῷ.
4:20.targetText: Then He rolled up the scroll, returned it to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English object of returned; the participle ἀποδούς has none.
English joins the participle series to "sat down".

4:21.sourceText: ἤρξατο δὲ λέγειν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Σήμερον πεπλήρωται ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν ὑμῶν.
4:21.targetText: and He began by saying, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

groups.note: ὠσίν ("ears") is rendered hearing.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves πρὸς αὐτούς ("to them") unrendered after saying.
The ὅτι introducing the quotation is represented only by the quotation marks.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:22.sourceText: καὶ πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς χάριτος τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον Οὐχὶ υἱός ἐστιν Ἰωσὴφ οὗτος;
4:22.targetText: All spoke well of Him and marveled at the gracious words that came from His lips. “Isn’t this the son of Joseph?” they asked.

groups.note: ἐμαρτύρουν ("bore witness") is rendered spoke well.
τῆς χάριτος ("of grace") is rendered gracious.
The article τοῖς with the participle ἐκπορευομένοις forms the relative clause.
Οὐχί … ἐστιν ("is not") is contracted to Isn’t.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB places "they asked" after the question and leaves καί unrendered.

4:23.sourceText: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς Πάντως ἐρεῖτέ μοι τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην Ἰατρέ, θεράπευσον σεαυτόν· ὅσα ἠκούσαμεν γενόμενα εἰς τὴν Καφαρναοὺμ, ποίησον καὶ ὧδε ἐν τῇ πατρίδι σου.
4:23.targetText: Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.’”

groups.note: The participle γενόμενα ("having happened") is recast as "that You did".

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves καί ("also") before ὧδε unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the verb ending.
English supplies the doer; γενόμενα only says the things happened.

4:24.sourceText: εἶπεν δέ Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς προφήτης δεκτός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ.
4:24.targetText: Then He added, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.

unmappedSource.reason: The ὅτι after "I tell you" is represented only by the comma.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:25.sourceText: ἐπ’ ἀληθείας δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, πολλαὶ χῆραι ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἡλείου ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτε ἐκλείσθη ὁ οὐρανὸς ἐπὶ ἔτη τρία καὶ μῆνας ἕξ, ὡς ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν,
4:25.targetText: But I tell you truthfully that there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and great famine swept over all the land.

groups.note: ἐπ’ ἀληθείας ("in truth") is rendered truthfully.
ἡμέραις ("days") is rendered time.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
μῆνας ἕξ ("six months") is rendered as the half year in "three and a half years".
ὡς ("when") is rendered and.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English introduces the statement; the Greek has no ὅτι here.

4:26.sourceText: καὶ πρὸς οὐδεμίαν αὐτῶν ἐπέμφθη Ἡλείας εἰ μὴ εἰς Σάρεπτα τῆς Σιδωνίας πρὸς γυναῖκα χήραν.
4:26.targetText: Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.

groups.note: οὐδεμίαν ("no one") is split into not … any.
Same name, spelled differently in BSB's Greek text.
εἰ μή ("except") is rendered but.
εἰς Σάρεπτα ("to Zarephath") is recast as the widow's town.
γυναῖκα χήραν ("a widow woman") is rendered the widow.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:27.sourceText: καὶ πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπὶ Ἑλισαίου τοῦ προφήτου, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκαθαρίσθη εἰ μὴ Ναιμὰν ὁ Σύρος.
4:27.targetText: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet. Yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.”

groups.note: ἐπί with the genitive ("in the time of") is rendered in the time.
εἰ μή ("except") is rendered only.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:28.sourceText: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες θυμοῦ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούοντες ταῦτα,
4:28.targetText: On hearing this, all the people in the synagogue were enraged.

groups.note: ἐπλήσθησαν θυμοῦ ("were filled with rage") is rendered were enraged.
The masculine plural πάντες ("all") implies people.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.

4:29.sourceText: καὶ ἀναστάντες ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἕως ὀφρύος τοῦ ὄρους ἐφ’ οὗ ἡ πόλις ᾠκοδόμητο αὐτῶν, ὥστε κατακρημνίσαι αὐτόν·
4:29.targetText: They got up, drove Him out of the town, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw Him over the cliff.

groups.note: ἔξω with the genitive ("outside of") is rendered out of.
ὥστε with the infinitive expresses purpose here.
κατακρημνίσαι ("to throw down a cliff") is rendered throw … over the cliff.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
BSB leaves αὐτῶν ("their") with town unrendered.

4:30.sourceText: αὐτὸς δὲ διελθὼν διὰ μέσου αὐτῶν ἐπορεύετο.
4:30.targetText: But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way.

groups.note: BSB renders αὐτός ("he") as Jesus.
μέσου αὐτῶν ("the midst of them") is rendered the crowd.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to "went on His way".

4:31.sourceText: Καὶ κατῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας. καὶ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν·
4:31.targetText: Then He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He began to teach the people.

groups.note: The periphrastic ἦν διδάσκων ("was teaching") is rendered began to teach.
BSB renders αὐτούς ("them") as the people.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:32.sourceText: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ ἦν ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ.
4:32.targetText: They were astonished at His teaching, because His message had authority.

groups.note: ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ ἦν ("was with authority") is rendered had authority.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

4:33.sourceText: καὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἦν ἄνθρωπος ἔχων πνεῦμα δαιμονίου ἀκαθάρτου, καὶ ἀνέκραξεν φωνῇ μεγάλῃ
4:33.targetText: In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,

groups.note: ἔχων ("having") is rendered possessed by.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves καί unrendered.

4:34.sourceText: Ἔα, τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ; ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς; οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ Ἅγιος τοῦ Θεοῦ.
4:34.targetText: “Ha! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”

groups.note: The idiom τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί ("what to us and to you?") is rendered What do You want with us.

studyHeads.note: σοί ("to you") is the one addressed.
ἡμῖν ("to us") is rendered with us.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies question support for the idiom; the Greek has no verb.
English verbalizes the idiom with want; the Greek has no verb of wanting.

4:35.sourceText: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ. καὶ ῥίψαν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον εἰς τὸ μέσον ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ μηδὲν βλάψαν αὐτόν.
4:35.targetText: But Jesus rebuked the demon. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!” At this, the demon threw the man down before them all and came out without harming him.

groups.note: BSB renders αὐτῷ ("him") as the demon.
ἀπ’ ("from") is rendered of; "out" belongs to ἔξελθε ("come out"), as with ἐξήρχετο ἀπό in 4:41.
BSB renders αὐτόν ("him") as the man.
εἰς τὸ μέσον ("into the middle") is rendered before them all.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB separates the two commands with "He said" and leaves καί unrendered.
BSB leaves ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ("from him") unrendered after came out.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to "came out".

4:36.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο θάμβος ἐπὶ πάντας, καὶ συνελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες Τίς ὁ λόγος οὗτος, ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ καὶ δυνάμει ἐπιτάσσει τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις πνεύμασιν καὶ ἐξέρχονται;
4:36.targetText: All the people were overcome with amazement and asked one another, “What is this message? With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”

groups.note: ἐγένετο θάμβος ἐπὶ πάντας ("amazement came upon all") is recast as all were overcome with amazement.
The masculine plural πάντας ("all") implies people.
πρὸς ἀλλήλους ("to one another") is rendered one another.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The participle λέγοντες ("saying") is represented only by the comma before the quotation.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here and leaves ὅτι ("that") unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: Supplied copula; the Greek question has no verb.

4:37.sourceText: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο ἦχος περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς πάντα τόπον τῆς περιχώρου.
4:37.targetText: And the news about Jesus spread throughout the surrounding region.

groups.note: BSB names Jesus for αὐτοῦ ("him").
εἰς πάντα τόπον ("into every place") is rendered throughout.

4:38.sourceText: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ἀπὸ τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος. πενθερὰ δὲ τοῦ Σίμωνος ἦν συνεχομένη πυρετῷ μεγάλῳ, καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν περὶ αὐτῆς.
4:38.targetText: After Jesus had left the synagogue, He went to the home of Simon, whose mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever. So they appealed to Jesus on her behalf,

groups.note: Ἀναστὰς ἀπό ("having risen from") is rendered as an after-clause with left.
τοῦ Σίμωνος ("of Simon") is rendered by the relative whose.
BSB renders αὐτόν ("him") as Jesus.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves δέ unrendered; After belongs to the participle.
BSB joins this sentence to the previous one with "whose" and leaves δέ unrendered.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names the subject; the Greek gives it only in the participle.

4:39.sourceText: καὶ ἐπιστὰς ἐπάνω αὐτῆς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πυρετῷ, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτήν· παραχρῆμα δὲ ἀναστᾶσα διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.
4:39.targetText: and He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. And she got up at once and began to serve them.

4:40.sourceText: Δύνοντος δὲ τοῦ ἡλίου ἅπαντες ὅσοι εἶχον ἀσθενοῦντας νόσοις ποικίλαις ἤγαγον αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτόν· ὁ δὲ ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπιτιθεὶς ἐθεράπευεν αὐτούς.
4:40.targetText: At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Jesus, and laying His hands on each one, He healed them.

groups.note: The genitive absolute Δύνοντος τοῦ ἡλίου ("as the sun was setting") is rendered At sunset.
ἀσθενοῦντας ("sick ones") is rendered were ill.
The active ἤγαγον ("they brought") is rendered with the passive were brought.
BSB names Jesus for αὐτόν ("him").
In ὁ δέ the article serves as the pronoun he.
The article τάς is rendered as the possessive His.

4:41.sourceText: ἐξήρχετο δὲ καὶ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ πολλῶν, κραυγάζοντα καὶ λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ. καὶ ἐπιτιμῶν οὐκ εἴα αὐτὰ λαλεῖν, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν τὸν Χριστὸν αὐτὸν εἶναι.
4:41.targetText: Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ.

4:42.sourceText: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἔρημον τόπον· καὶ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπεζήτουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἦλθον ἕως αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατεῖχον αὐτὸν τοῦ μὴ πορεύεσθαι ἀπ’ αὐτῶν.
4:42.targetText: At daybreak, Jesus went out to a solitary place, and the crowds were looking for Him. They came to Him and tried to keep Him from leaving.
